INTEGRATED SCIENCE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

4. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

5. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.

7. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Heating until a solid melts

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.

9. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

10. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Paper burning to ash

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. newton (N)
   D. pascal (Pa)

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.

17. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Only carbon dioxide

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
18. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
